title: Exactness of finite direct image
statement:
For finite $f$, the functor $f_*:\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ is exact.
Consequently $R^qf_*=0$ for $q>0$ and $Rf_*=f_*$ on $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$.

proof.text: For the original etale-sheaf declarations attached to this node, use the finite geometric-stalk formula: the pushforward stalk is a finite sum of source stalks, hence exact. Geometric stalks are conservative. These declarations are unchanged by E3.

For the attached WeilSheaf.isZero_higherLowerStar_of_isFinite declaration, work with the actual pro-etale AdicSheaf implementation. The geometric-fibre map q of p is finite and locally of finite presentation: the target is locally Noetherian because it is locally of finite type over a field, and these morphism properties survive base change. A finite pullback of Spec R for w-contractible R is affine, say Spec S, and S is module-finite and finitely presented over R. Apply the finite w-contractibility theorem to S.

Cover every target pro-etale object by affine opens, and each affine open by the faithfully flat ind-etale w-contractible algebra of exists_isWContractibleRing. Compose the two coverings. This is the construction in the already proved Scheme.ProEt.exists_isWeaklyContractible_cover, retaining the ring witness. By Scheme.ProEt.isWeaklyContractible_of_iso each cover member and its finite pullback are weakly contractible. Apply GrothendieckTopology.exact_iff_of_forall_exists and exact evaluation on weakly contractible objects. Evaluation of the direct image equals evaluation on its pullback, so direct image preserves homology and finite colimits. All this is Lean-proved in private helpers of the item.

Reflect finite-colimit preservation from ordinary module sheaves through AdicSheaf.forget, then transfer it to Frobenius-equivariant sheaves with Endofunctor.IsoAlgebra.preservesFiniteColimits_mapOfNatIso. The exact functor comparison singleFunctorCompRightDerivedFunctorIso identifies the derived direct image of a degree-zero object with a degree-zero object. Positive-degree homology of the latter vanishes by DerivedCategory.isZero_of_isLE, and the comparison transports this vanishing to the stated Weil higher direct image.

proof_origin.place: Original etale finite-stalk proof retained; E3 stage-3 proof of the attached WeilSheaf vanishing uses finite w-contractible pullbacks (Stacks 0986) and exact evaluation, followed by the exact derived-functor comparison. No unit-level route is changed.

blueprint_sketch.statement: If $h$ is finite, then $h_*$ on etale abelian sheaves is exact.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
For a short exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$, apply the stalk
formula at every geometric $\bar v$. A finite product of short exact
sequences of abelian groups is exact, so the sequence of stalks of the direct
images is exact. Geometric stalks are conservative for etale sheaves:
injectivity and surjectivity can be checked after an etale neighbourhood of
each geometric point and then sheafified. Hence the direct-image sequence is
exact. Consequently the total right derived functor $Rh_*$ is $h_*$ applied levelwise to
complexes, and in particular $R^qh_*=0$ for $q>0$; only the first of these two consequences
is formalised.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes and let $\mathcal A$ be a
Grothendieck abelian coefficient category for which presheaves on small etale
sites can be sheafified, which is concrete over sets with a forgetful functor
that reflects isomorphisms, preserves filtered colimits and is compatible with
the sheaf condition on $Y_{\Et}$ (for instance $\mathcal A=\Mod_\Lambda$).
Then the direct image $f_*:\shv{X_{\Et},\mathcal A}\to\shv{Y_{\Et},\mathcal A}$
is exact. Consequently, whenever the derived categories of $\mathcal A$-valued
etale sheaves on $X$ and $Y$ exist and every complex of sheaves on $X$ has a
K-injective resolution, the total right derived functor $Rf_*$ is isomorphic
to $f_*$ applied termwise to complexes; in particular $R^qf_*=0$ for $q>0$.

proof.text:
*Left exactness.* By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image],
$(f_*G)(V)=G(X\times_YV)$ for $V\to Y$ etale. Kernels of sheaves in the
abelian category $\shv{X_{\Et},\mathcal A}$ (and in
$\shv{Y_{\Et},\mathcal A}$) are computed sectionwise, so $f_*$ preserves
kernels and finite products, i.e. finite limits.

*Epimorphisms.* Let $\varphi:G\to G'$ be an epimorphism of $\mathcal A$-valued
sheaves on $X_{\Et}$. For $s\in Y$ let $\bar s$ be the geometric point of $Y$ at
an algebraic closure of $\kappa(s)$. Geometric stalks are colimits, so they
preserve epimorphisms, and by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] (which
applies since $\overline{\kappa(s)}$ is algebraically closed) the map
$(f_*\varphi)_{\bar s}$ is identified, naturally in $\varphi$, with
$\prod_{\bar x}\varphi_{\bar x}:\prod_{\bar x}G_{\bar x}\to\prod_{\bar x}G'_{\bar x}$,
the product running over the finite geometric fibre [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre]
of $f$ over $\bar s$. A finite product of epimorphisms in the abelian category
$\mathcal A$ is an epimorphism, so $(f_*\varphi)_{\bar s}$ is an epimorphism for
every $s\in Y$. Let $c:f_*G'\to Q$ be the cokernel of $f_*\varphi$. Stalks
commute with cokernels, so $Q_{\bar s}=0$ for every $s$, and the map $0\to Q$
is an isomorphism on all these geometric stalks; by
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] (its hypotheses on $\mathcal A$
are among ours, and these geometric points are universe-raised as in
[lemma-openclosed-point-ulift]) it is an isomorphism, so $Q=0$ and
$f_*\varphi$ is an epimorphism.

A left exact functor between abelian categories which preserves epimorphisms
preserves homology, hence finite colimits; so $f_*$ is exact.

*Derived functor.* Let $K$ be a complex of $\mathcal A$-valued sheaves on $X$ and
$K\to I$ a K-injective resolution. Then $Rf_*K=f_*I$, and since $f_*$ is exact
it carries the quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ to a quasi-isomorphism
$f_*K\to f_*I$. These quasi-isomorphisms are natural in $K$, so they give an
isomorphism between $Rf_*$ and $f_*$ applied termwise. For a sheaf $F$ placed
in degree $0$, $R^qf_*F=H^q(f_*F)=0$ for $q>0$.
